DEWORMING DUE 

All 470 tests pass, test docs cleaned up. Final summary:

Code (reminder_alerts.py): GroomingDueAlert now resolves real clinic_name/city_name via ClinicRepo (reusing the exact same repo methods AppointmentAlert already uses elsewhere), passes clinic_id through for redirection. 5 new/updated tests, all passing.

Config (quick_commerce.alerts, both GROOMING_DUE_REMINDER and GROOMING_OVERDUE_REMINDER): static "Due"/"Overdue" badge, "{pet}'s Next Grooming" heading, "Trained Groomer" + due-date row, resolved city/clinic row, two CTAs (Rebook + View Details), grooming discount banner — 10% off vaccination claim intentionally left out per your call.

Bug found and fixed along the way: a duplicate GROOMING_DUE_REMINDER config doc was silently shadowing updates (AlertsRepo has no duplicate-name handling) — you deleted it, confirmed clean now, and confirmed no other duplicated names exist anywhere in the collection.

Verified live, not just unit-tested: injected a real test reminder, ran the actual GroomingDueAlert.build() against real dev Postgres/Mongo, got back a fully-formed card matching the target design field-for-field — real clinic ("Vetic, Sector 57, Gurugram"), real due date, two working CTAs.

Still deliberately deferred: the specific suggested time slot (no "next available slot" capability exists anywhere in the codebase — flagged earlier as a separate, bigger piece of work, per your instruction to leave it).

Still the actual blocker for this to ever appear for a real user: the underlying clinic_org.app_alerts.GroomingReminder feed is still dead (no writes since 2026-03-10) — none of today's work changes that; it just means the alert is now fully correct and ready the moment that feed comes back or gets replaced.

medicing refill


Your understanding is correct. Here's the full picture:

Who creates the reminders — not us, a separate job:
Every MEDICINE_REFILL doc in vetic_vms.reminders has created_by: "Medicine Reminder Service" and source: "INVOICE". That, plus the medicine_reminder_config collection I found (per-category rules like Kiwof: {per_unit_cyclicity_days: 91, overdue_expiry_days: 30}), confirms it: there's an external batch job (a cron, not living in this repo) that periodically scans purchase/invoice history, checks each category's repurchase cycle from medicine_reminder_config, and writes a reminder doc when a customer is due. Our qc_order_service code — old and new — only reads what that job already produced. We never compute "is this medicine due" ourselves.

The query and what $gte/$lte mean (epharmacy_alerts.py:279-281 → medicine_reminder_repository.py:11-19):


start_date = (today - 7 days).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")   # e.g. "2026-08-27"
end_date   = (today + 7 days).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")   # e.g. "2026-09-10"

"due_date": {"$gte": start_date, "$lte": end_date}
$gte = "greater than or equal to", $lte = "less than or equal to" — standard Mongo comparison operators. So the filter says: find reminders whose due_date falls between 7 days ago and 7 days from now (inclusive both ends) — a 14-day window centered on today. Since due_date is stored as a plain "YYYY-MM-DD" string, Mongo compares it lexicographically (character by character) rather than as a real date — but that happens to sort identically to chronological order precisely because ISO format is zero-padded and year-first, so it works correctly here.

What I actually built, seeded, and tested:

Added the MEDICINE_REFILL config doc to dev's quick_commerce.alerts collection (priority 37, a free slot right after UNPAID_PARTIAL_BILL/RX_PENDING_PLACE_ORDER), reusing the unpaid_bill template/theme since it's the closest existing shape and is already proven to render on the client — heading, CTA, and status match variables()'s actual output keys.
Fixed a real gap while testing: pet_id wasn't being threaded through, so per-pet dedup/suppression wouldn't have scoped correctly — now fixed and covered by a test.
Ran it live against real dev data (not mocks) — found an actual due Bravecto reminder for a real user/pet and confirmed the full pipeline (Mongo fetch → variant resolution → config render → response) end-to-end:
title: "SAND's Bravecto refill due", subtitle = real product name, pet_id populated, CTA "Order Now" → screen_id 18 with the right vetic_variant_id.
All 466 unit/integration tests pass (5 pre-existing test_api.py failures are an unrelated httpx/starlette version mismatch, confirmed present before my changes too).
This is dev-only — nothing pushed yet. Want me to commit this, or do you want to eyeball/tweak the config doc's colors/copy first?


Abondoned cart



  1. Core fix — generalize _eta_text() (commerce_alerts.py:50-54): instead of regex-hunting for a "\d+ mins" substring (which only matches the open-clinic phrasing and silently passes closed-clinic text through unchanged), strip the "Get it " prefix from whatever qc_delivery_text says and capitalize what's left. This works for both shapes without hardcoding each one:

    • "Get it in 45 mins" → "In 45 mins" (same as today)
    • "Get it by Tomorrow 9:00 AM" → "By Tomorrow 9:00 AM" (currently broken)
    • "Get it by 9:00 AM" → "By 9:00 AM" (currently broken)

    This is future-proof too — if the phrasing in get_time_for_distance_and_opening ever changes, _eta_text doesn't need a matching regex update.

  2. Adjacent bug worth folding in — get_dynamic_delivery_text() (app/utils.py:2385) returns a bare " " (single space) when no clinics are found for the pincode. That's a truthy string, so _eta_text's if not delivery_text guard won't catch it — the alert title would render as just a blank space. Fix: return default_delivery_str there instead of " ", so the fallback "In 30 mins" kicks in consistently.

  3. Test coverage: add cases to _eta_text (or wherever tested) for the closed-clinic ("Get it by...") and no-clinic (empty/whitespace) inputs — currently only the happy-path "In X mins" case is implicitly covered.

Want me to go ahead and implement this?

added qc check only show commerce alerts

What changed

The gate — base_alert_service.py gains allowed_categories (explicit constructor arg, not a ctx key) and _eligible_classes(), which filters the registry on cls.alert_category before instantiation. get_alerts builds from that instead of the raw registry.

The declaration — base_page.py gets allowed_categories: set[str] | None = None plus an _alert_service() helper. Pages collect through the helper, so a new screen only sets the one class attribute — there's no second place to remember, and no way to forget to pass it. shop_page.py declares {"commerce"}; home_page.py stays None.

The plumbing — alert_service.py forwards it via _primary() / _sticky(). dismiss_sticky_alert deliberately doesn't get it: its docstring says dismissal isn't screen-scoped, and it never touches the registry.

The subtle fix — sticky_alert_service.py:175 _candidate_alert_names now iterates _eligible_classes(). Without this, a commerce-restricted shop poll would list appointment strips as hideable and flip their rows invisible on every request — the exact home/shop row-flipping bug its own docstring warns about.

Zero method-signature churn: screen is already threaded through ~9 signatures, and I didn't want to double that, so the allowlist rides the constructor where it belongs (fixed for the whole request, same lifetime as user_id).

Result

screenallowedprimary buildssticky builds
home(none)62/6210/10
shop{"commerce"}19/624/10
vms(none)——

Shop drops 43 primary + 6 sticky fetches per request — those alerts now never run their fetch(), rather than fetching and being discarded.

None vs set() are kept distinct (is None, not a falsy check), so a future screen declaring set() shows nothing instead of silently falling back to everything. vms is untouched — its collect() still returns [] directly, so it never reaches the service.

Verification

  • 495 passed. The 1 failure + 4 errors in test_api.py are pre-existing — a starlette/httpx TestClient.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'app' incompatibility. I confirmed identical results on a stashed clean tree.
  • 13 new tests in test_page_category_scoping.py, written against the real registries so they keep holding as alerts land. Both mutations caught: disabling the gate fails 7; reverting just the _candidate_alert_names fix fails the row-flipping guard specifically.
  • One test is a standing guard that every registered class declares a non-empty alert_category — since the gate is fail-closed, a class without one would be silently dropped from every restricted screen. All 72 currently declare one.
  • The key behavioral test proves the page wins over the config: an appointment alert with screen_page: ["home", "shop"] explicitly set still cannot reach shop.

Two things to know before deploying

This removes alerts from the shop page that are probably showing right now. screen_page appears in no seed script in the repo — only in test fixtures — so I'd expect most live configs lack it, meaning shop is currently leaking all five clusters. Worth a quick count against the live alerts collection so you know what disappears.

The boundary matches legacy, which is what makes it safe: legacy shop's one reminder call was get_reminders_v4(..., is_shop_page_alert=True) → FoodReminder only, and FOOD_DUE_REMINDER is a CommerceAlert. The clinical reminders correctly stay on home.

I made your two open judgment calls the low-risk way: epharmacy keeps its existing commerce tag (2 alerts — unpaid partial bill, Rx pending; both genuinely shop-shaped), and VmsPage is untouched. Say the word if you want either different — epharmacy is now a one-line change on its cluster base.

2. Booking kar li ho to card na dikhe — reminder_repo.py:73-85

Suppression ab service_type_id padhta hai. Sirf DocReminder ke liye — vaccination/deworming ka check jaan-boojh ke chhod diya (usme wahi bug hai, par usse on karna ek alag behaviour change hai apne blast radius ke saath). Comment me likh diya hai.

3. check_last_visit wapas — booking_repo.py:152 + reminder_alerts.py:119

Junk PetID (nan/null/khaali) pe last visit se asli pet nikaalta hai. Purchases exclude — product kharidna visit nahi hai. Per-request memoised, to dono doctor alerts ek hi query me kaam chalate hain.

4. Deep-link ki date — due_date_iso add kiya

{due_date} display form hai ("06 Sep 2026") aur wahi booking screen ko date param me ja raha tha, jahan legacy raw "2026-09-06" bhejta tha — date pre-fill chupchaap fail ho rahi thi. Ab dono variables alag hain.

5. Blank ReminderName ka fallback — "Follow-up visit" / "Post-surgery check". Config ka {reminder_name} subtitle khaali ya "nan" render ho raha tha.

Ek gap test ne pakda: "nan" khaali nahi hota, to mera pehla version usse pet_id me survive karne deta — deep-link aur card identity dono me junk id chali jati. Ab invalid PetID hamesha replace hota hai (khaali se bhi), aur build() khaali redirection keys strip kar deta hai (gift card ka wahi pattern)
